newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt police kill two Moslem militants in south.
newsitem.headline: Egypt police kill two Moslem militants in south.

text.p: Egyptian police shot dead two suspected Moslem militants on Tuesday in a raid on a southern village, security sources said.
They said police were tipped off that militants from the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) were hiding in Kafr Abdel Khaleq province in Minya province, some 235 km (150 miles) south of Cairo.
Police and militants exchanged fire and Hassan Abdel Mawlah and Saleh Mahmoud -- identified by police as leading members of the Gama'a -- were killed, the sources said.
The Interior Ministry said the two men were charged with raiding jewelry shops, banks and stealing a police rifle from the nearby Beni Suef police station.
Police also found two automatic rifles and 10,000 pounds ($2,900) beside the two bodies.

Since 1992, the Gama'a has been fighting a low-intensity guerrilla war to overthrow the government and set up a strict Islamic state. Police raids have contained their activities to Egypt's southern provinces. Almost 1,000 people have been killed in the conflict.
